question: An electromagnetic wave has frequency $6.0 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}$ and travels in vacuum. Calculate its wavelength. Also explain why the wave can travel without any material medium.

options.A: $\lambda=\dfrac{\nu}{c}=2.0\times10^6\text{ m}$. The wave needs air because electric and magnetic fields cannot exist in vacuum.
options.B: $\lambda=5.0\times10^{-7}\text{ m}$. The wave travels in vacuum because its electric field alone carries the disturbance; the magnetic field is not involved.
options.C:
$\lambda=\dfrac{c}{\nu}=\dfrac{3.0\times10^8}{6.0\times10^{14}}=5.0\times10^{-7}\text{ m}$.
An electromagnetic wave can travel without a material medium because its time-varying electric field produces a magnetic field and its time-varying magnetic field produces an electric field; the fields sustain the propagating disturbance.
options.D: $\lambda=5.0\times10^{-7}\text{ m}$. The wave propagates without a medium because all waves travel faster in vacuum, irrespective of their nature.
